verified_integrations.name: tftp-parser-differential-conformance
verified_integrations.scope: Real-process differential conformance for toy_tcpip::tftp::TftpPacket::parse against an independent Python oracle, covering reviewed valid/malformed TFTP packets plus a deterministic exhaustive single-bit mutation schedule over representative RRQ, ACK, and ERROR seeds.
verification_contract: Rust 1.88 adapter formatting and Clippy -D warnings
build the adapter against the imported toy_tcpip crate
ruff-check the independent oracle and integration tests
DifferentialHarness executes the Rust candidate and Python oracle as real subprocess targets
reviewed valid and malformed TFTP corpus must produce equivalent canonical semantic results
DeterministicByteMutations plus run_fuzz_campaign must exhaust the representative single-bit mutation schedule without a product mismatch or infrastructure failure
limitations: does not claim whole-stack or whole-RFC TFTP conformance
does not exercise UDP sockets, packet transport, file transfer, or TFTP server behavior
does not prove MinIOS networking or container networking interoperability
does not make security or performance claims

verified_integrations.name: hypervisor-minios-early-boot
verified_integrations.scope: Real-KVM early MinIOS kernel boot using the imported mini-hypervisor public VM/vCPU/memory/debug-port APIs. The integration builds the real MinIOS ELF32 kernel, loads PT_LOAD segments, executes a guest-owned real-to-protected-mode Multiboot v1 bridge, reaches kernel_main and the exact debug banner, then proves the next execution boundary is the first intentionally unsupported PIC-remap OUT 0x20 access.
verification_contract: build the real imported MinIOS kernel.bin ELF32 artifact with the 32-bit freestanding toolchain
assemble and link a bounded guest-owned Multiboot bridge below the 64 KiB real-mode window
Rust 1.74 formatting, Clippy -D warnings, and harness build against the imported mini-hypervisor crate
require a real /dev/kvm execution rather than a mocked vCPU or synthetic exit
parse and load the MinIOS ELF32 PT_LOAD segments into registered guest memory and pass Multiboot magic 0x2BADB002 plus a minimal valid memory-info structure
require the exact MinIOS debug-port proof Booting Advanced OS... followed by the exact first unsupported PIC boundary OUT port 0x20 size 1 count 1
limitations: proves early MinIOS kernel boot only through the first legacy PIC I/O boundary
does not claim PIC, PIT, keyboard, ATA, interrupt, shell, filesystem, or networking device support under mini-hypervisor
does not claim a complete MinIOS boot or interactive userspace session
does not make security or performance claims
